events.title: Annexation of Chau O and Chau Ly into Dai Viet
events.description: King Che Man of Champa offered the two prefectures of O and Ly as a wedding gift to marry Princess Huyen Tran of the Tran Dynasty. The land of Thua Thien Hue officially became the territory of Dai Viet, and was later renamed Hoa Chau.

events.title: Lord Nguyen Phuc Thai moved the lord's residence to Phu Xuan
events.description: Lord Nguyen Phuc Thai (Lord Nghia) decided to move the capital of Dang Trong from Kim Long to Phu Xuan village. This event marked the beginning of Hue's status as a political center throughout subsequent dynasties.

events.title: Nguyen Hue ascended the throne as Emperor
events.description: At Ban Mountain (south of Phu Xuan Citadel), King Bac Binh Nguyen Hue set up an altar to worship Heaven and Earth, officially ascended the throne as Emperor, taking the reign name Quang Trung, before marching north to defeat the Qing army.

events.title: Gia Long established the capital in Phu Xuan
events.description: After defeating the Tay Son Dynasty and unifying the country, Nguyen Anh ascended the throne as Emperor (Gia Long), choosing Phu Xuan (Hue) as the capital of unified Vietnam, beginning the large-scale construction of the Hue Citadel.

events.title: The counter-attack at Hue Citadel (The Fall of the Capital)
events.description: The war faction of the Nguyen court, led by Ton That Thuyet, opened fire on the French barracks at Mang Ca post and the French Resident Superior's Office. The attack failed, and the French army counter-attacked, capturing the Citadel and massacring the population. King Ham Nghi had to abandon the throne, flee to Tan So, and issue the Can Vuong edict.

events.title: Establishment of the Thua Thien Hue Province Party Committee
events.description: The conference to establish the Thua Thien Hue Province Party Committee of the Communist Party of Vietnam was held in secret, marking an important turning point in the revolutionary movement at the nerve center of the colonial-feudal regime.

events.title: King Bao Dai abdicated
events.description: At the Ngu Phung Pavilion (Ngo Mon Gate), King Bao Dai handed over the imperial seal and sword to the representative of the Provisional Government, Mr. Tran Huy Lieu, declaring 'I would rather be a citizen of an independent country than a king of an enslaved nation', ending thousands of years of feudalism in Vietnam.

events.title: The Tet Offensive (Hue Front)
events.description: The Liberation Army launched simultaneous attacks and controlled Hue City for 26 days and nights. The flag of the National Liberation Front flew atop the Phu Van Lau flagpole. This was the most fierce urban battle, creating a great resonance worldwide but also leaving behind much grief.

events.title: Liberation of Thua Thien Hue
events.description: During the Hue - Da Nang Campaign, the 2nd Corps and local armed forces attacked and shattered the defense system of the Saigon army. The liberation flag was raised to the top of Ky Dai at 6:30 AM, marking the complete liberation of the Ancient Capital.

events.title: Re-establishment of Thua Thien Hue Province
events.description: The 8th National Assembly passed a Resolution to split Binh Tri Thien Province (merged since 1976) back into 3 provinces: Quang Binh, Quang Tri, and Thua Thien Hue. Thua Thien Hue Province began a new phase of development based on culture and tourism.
